title: Regular-center blowups and transforms under Tor-independent base change
statement:
Let $g:X'\to X$ be a morphism of Noetherian schemes and let $V\hookrightarrow X$ be a regular closed immersion, meaning its ideal is locally generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], with the empty sequence allowed. Write $V'=X'\times_XV$, and let $I,I'$ be the respective ideals. Say that a closed subscheme $F\hookrightarrow X$ is Tor independent of $X'$ over $X$ if, on affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $F=V(J)$, $\operatorname{Tor}^{A}_i(A',A/J)=0$ for every $i>0$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Suppose $V$ is Tor independent of $X'$. Then $V'\hookrightarrow X'$ is regular and the canonical maps $g^*(I^a)\to(I')^a$ are isomorphisms for every $a\geq0$. In particular
$$\operatorname{Bl}_{V'}X'\cong X'\times_X\operatorname{Bl}_V X,$$
where blowup means the scheme obtained locally as $\operatorname{Proj}\bigoplus_{a\geq0}I^a$.

Let $W\hookrightarrow X$ be another regular closed immersion with $V\times_XW\hookrightarrow W$ regular. Put $W'=X'\times_XW$. If $W$ and $V\times_XW$ are also Tor independent of $X'$, then the induced immersion $V'\times_{X'}W'\hookrightarrow W'$ is regular and
$$ (W')^{\rm st}\cong X'\times_X W^{\rm st}.$$
Strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure of the inverse image away from $V$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. For a finite normal crossings divisor $W=\sum_j W_j$ on a regular $X$, with $X'$ regular and $W'=g^*W$ a normal crossings divisor, the same strict-transform identity holds for $W$ if these hypotheses hold for every nonempty intersection of its components and for its intersection with $V$. Here every $W_j$ is an effective Cartier divisor, every nonempty intersection of distinct components is regular of the expected codimension, and the sums are reduced Cartier divisors.
